utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It was Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Antic. On Friday, the last series of questions was related to certain members of the 4th Detachment. In the same context, I would like to ask you whether Stanko Dujkovic was also a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Stanko Dujkovic was indeed a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you perhaps remember in the night between the 16th and the 17th of April, what was his duty? What was his task as member of the 4th Detachment? Where was he exactly?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanko Dujkovic did not have any specific duty in the 4th Detachment. He must have been in his flat, at his home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Antic: Darko Misic, was he also a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Vlado Sisic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was also a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A man named Dusanovic, nicknamed Dzaltara, who was a well-known football player in Samac, was he too a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was quite a well-known football player in the area of Samac municipality, and yes, he was a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many snipers did the 4th Detachment have deployed along the roofs of buildings on the 16th, in the evening?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment had no snipers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue an order to Dzaltara to cut the phone lines at 3.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sisic receive from you the order to take the memorial centre and the radio station?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Darko Misic receive from you the order to take the Silos?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he receive orders from anyone else?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. He couldn't have received orders from anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ivanovski Sarinic and Topcagic, were they actually the ones who brought the volunteers to Samac on the 16th and the 17th, the volunteers and the Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about Fadil Topcagic's case. He spoke to me in passing at the command of the 4th Detachment, when Mr. Zaric and I started out towards Pelagicevo. In passing, that is, later actually, he told me what had happened in Samac. He made a passing comment on that. And he told me that he had been taken forcibly to perform such a mission by the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the SDS make any plans with the 4th Detachment prior to the 16th of April concerning the takeover in Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment never had anything to do with the SDS concerning any such events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment and you, as its commander, did you have any contacts with Blagoje Simic concerning plans of a takeover?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained that after your removal, or however you choose to refer to it, you were performing the duties of a commander who had the obligation to build bunkers. You told us that you looked after people there. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Antic, you, as an educated man, a man with an amount of military education, you will not dispute the fact that each commander, within his zone of responsibility, has a certain responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every soldier is given his own individual task while on duty and performing a certain mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think you've understood me right. I'm talking about commanders of military units. Within the zone, the area of responsibility of his unit, he has all the responsibility; isn't that correct, according to the military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I must elaborate on this. When a military unit occupies a certain area or, more specifically, when the 4th Detachment reached the line of its responsibility, that were the embankments, then the commander and the unit, if on duty, are in charge of that particular period of time while they are on duty, or else you appoint a commander of the line, and then this commander is in charge of the whole stretch, of the whole length of the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were commander of the 4th Detachment, according to military doctrine, you were responsible for everything in the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander is responsible for the specific task which he received from the Superior Command. He is in charge of carrying out this specific task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More specifically, the 17th Tactical Group gives you a task to secure the river banks of the Bosna and the Sava Rivers and you said Samac was your area of responsibility. That was the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment and you as commander, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise, the area of responsibility of the commander of the 17th Tactical Group covers the broad area in which the 17th Tactical Group was active. Nikolic was responsible for that, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the Superior Command, the command of the 17th Tactical Group would have been responsible for the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment too, that is, the command of the 4th Detachment would be in charge of carrying out the tasks given by the command of the 17th Tactical Group and would be responsible for the area in which the command of the 4th Detachment is in charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were responsible for the people who were working with you building the bunkers. You looked after them and you protected them from any military operations.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in charge of their personal safety. I was responsible for their personal safety. I was there with them the whole time, exposed to enemy fire, just like they were, possible enemy fire. I made sure that nothing happened to them which might put their lives in danger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise, any other people who went to Grebnice or to another line of the front would have been within the responsibility of whoever was the commander there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The line of responsibility later occupied by the 5th Battalion, when the JNA had been reorganised, that is, the 4th Detachment; but while I was the commander, the line of responsibility for Grebnice was not within the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I'm saying. It was someone else's responsibility, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment, after the JNA had reorganised and after the army of Republika Srpska had been set up, the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment was extended to include the area of Grebnice. But this happened at a later stage, after the army had been reorganised and after the army of Republika Srpska had been set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, you will agree, as far as the people who were assigned their work obligation to work for the army are concerned, whether it was bunkers or some other activity, the commander of the military unit would have been responsible for them? I'm asking you in general about such cases, like you were responsible at the embankment.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of responsibility was the responsibility of the army, and the army secured conditions for the safety of their unit's members, as far as any possible involvement is concerned, there were certain people in charge of that, people from -- who were working in other bodies too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, someone with a work assignment is digging a trench in another position, not necessarily on the Sava River bank. Who would be responsible for that man digging the trench?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever got him involved in that particular task, whoever gave him that particular work assignment would have been responsible for that man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to draw a parallel. For example, you were responsible for people who were working on the bunkers, and then would another military commander have been responsible for the people digging the trenches? Just tell me yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Access to responsibilities must not absolutely be according to the same criteria. I am a person who feels responsible. I consider myself a responsible person. I looked after those people. I looked after those people. What happened in other places, I'm really not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But based on the general military doctrine, everything that you were taught as a military officer, is there any responsibility involved under the military regulations, under the Geneva Conventions? You must have been taught that at some point.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did study all the international regulations governing such cases. Engagement of persons in such tasks was not the responsibility of military units or military officers, military commanders. It was down to personal responsibility. I considered myself responsible as a human being to look after those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't consider yourself responsible in your capacity as a military officer responsible for those people?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I considered myself as a human being responsible for protecting those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were not duty-bound or bound by law, in terms of responsibility for the people working there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must point out again that the responsible person is whoever gets those people involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, you talked about violations of the law by the volunteers and by the Serbian police, immediately following the armed clashes in the night between the 16th and the 17th. You remember, don't you? As commander of the 4th Detachment, why did you not simply arrest those people, if you knew that they were committing a crime?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As commander of the 4th Detachment, I could not make arrests. I did not have the authority to do so, because the 4th Detachment does not contain a unit of military police. The military police can do it and they can arrest their own members. So certainly the civilian authorities would have been in charge of such -- any such action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, tell me, please: If you had this information, why didn't you -- did you forward this to the commander of the Tactical Group, Colonel -- Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic? Did you ask him to send over military police and arrest those people who had committed crimes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed the command of the 17th Tactical Group about everything that was going on in Samac. I was not in a position as a lower-ranking commander to give any orders to the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, who is above the command of the 4th Detachment. It is up to him to assess the situation and take any steps or get his own MP unit involved. This is a strictly defined procedure in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Be that as it may, despite your reports, the command of the 17th Tactical Group never arrested those volunteers, did they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 17th Tactical Group would assess the situation probably. I was never present when they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please no hearsay. Tell us what you know from your own personal experience. Don't speculate. You either know or you don't.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the five or six days while I was commander, I don't know that any of those people had committed those crimes were actually arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue the order for the tanks to enter the town in the night between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this issued by the Superior Command? Who issued the command?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: At 3.00 in the morning on the 17th of April, 1992, you woke up. I can see that a lot of people were sleeping at that time. Please tell me: Until 5.30, as you said, when you went to the command at Pelagicevo, what did you do from 3.00 a.m. to 5.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard shooting. When I looked at the clock, it was 3.00 a.m., and I needed at least 15 or 20 minutes to get ready. Of course, when I arrived at the command, since I issued an order to the duty officer at the command to call in the command, the majority of the command members had already arrived, because they were all close to the command, as far as the place of their residence is concerned. I arrived among the last, because my apartment is the farthest away. At that point, it wasn't easy to move around or to reach the command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you spent about two hours at the 4th Detachment command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I got there at about 3.30, to the command, and I left at 4.30, it means that I spent about one hour at the command. During that hour, we informed ourselves about all the information that had reached the command regarding the situation in Samac, and I've already told you who was the one who actually provided this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my conclusion that you just sat at the command and did nothing is right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did actually happen? Did you take part in any military actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no military actions, because, as I said, I already said how the events evolved. It was, of course, an unpredictable situation for the command, and in a certain way it was a large shock for the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me: The proclamation by the 4th Command [as interpreted], when was that issued?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command proclamation was issued on the 19th, over the radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told my colleague Pisarevic that this proclamation was the pride of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It was the pride of the 4th Detachment because it called on all of the Samac citizens to join the 4th Detachment in protecting the people and their property, and in order to prevent any ill deeds that had been committed over those two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, since you actually compiled this proclamation as the command of the 4th Detachment, I don't mean just you, everything that is in that, absolutely every word in the proclamation is true; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The command actively participated in putting together this proclamation, and as I said, this was stylistically processed or done by Mr. Zaric because he was the security organ. Of course, in that part, there were certain views which were a little bit of an illusion, i.e. we were of the view at the command and we stood by that view throughout the whole period, and that is the view that the 4th Detachment should be of mixed composition, that all citizens should take part in it to protect the lives of people, because of course a person is only born once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, there are no lies; everything in the proclamation is true?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is our view.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Registrar, could we have Exhibit D28/4 ter for Mr. Antic. I would like to discuss this exhibit with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have something that I would like to read to you, and could you please tell me whether you agree with that or not. "The mainstay of this defensive view and the desire of it was the legendary 4th Detachment, which, as part of the reserve forces of the JNA, along with other detachments from this region, was part of the 17th Tactical Group. The detachment was mixed, representing members of all of the three ethnic groups which lived in the town and its task was in this micro-territory to prevent any occurrences or conflicts which could bring into question the survival of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a part of that, to prevent interethnic conflicts in town and also the spreading of the conflict to this area." Do you agree with what I have just read to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of this were specific tasks of the 4th Detachment. That is the transfer of combat activities from the Republic of Croatia to Bosnia and Herzegovina [as interpreted], and in that aspect, we believe that the 4th Detachment partially carried out its task, because in that area of the Samac municipality --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, let me just interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that this needs a bit of clarification. Maybe it was misinterpretation. On page 11, when the witness answered: "A part of this were specific tasks of the 4th Detachment. That is the transfer of combat activities from the Republic of Croatia to Bosnia and Herzegovina." I believe that this is something missing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will clarify that with the witness. Obviously, this is not what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I'm asking you specifically what I have just read to you, do you agree with that or do you not agree with that? Could you please just answer that. Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am talking about things that relate to the 4th Detachment, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please take this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Usher, please, you can just leave the document in front of the witness, because I have to discuss a little bit with him, and you can take your seat. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will read a part of that, and could you please tell me whether you agree with that or not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note. We do not have a copy of this document, D28/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe the interpreters' booth can get one copy so that we can facilitate proceedings, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "By carrying out their combat operations and tasks, the 4th Samac Detachment, as an armed force of all the nations [as interpreted] and ethnic groups which live in Bosanski Samac, has taken upon itself the honourable responsibility for freedom, order, work, a normal life, and the dignity of each man, regardless of his faith, ethnic group, social origin, or political convictions." You agree with that, and this is something that the 4th Detachment implemented; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like to clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment considers the carrying out of its tasks going to the line of the area of responsibility during the 17th. Before that, the 4th Detachment did not have any military tasks. So this exclusively refers to carrying out the tasks which we received from the higher command, the command of the 17th Tactical Group, i.e. for the 4th Detachment to go to the line of its area of responsibility and to secure it so that no other military force from the other side can enter Samac. So that was our first combat task, and I would like to emphasise that in carrying out this task, we also suffered some casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can agree, Mr. Antic: From the 17th onward, you agree that this was the role of the 4th Detachment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We believed --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, please. Could you just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must clarify. You cannot look at it in just a one-sided manner. We considered that by carrying out this combat task, we created conditions for the citizens to be safe, for their lives not to be threatened, that nobody would abuse them, nobody would rob their property or loot. This is what we believed to be the essence of our task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to secure peace and order and normal work?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a general principle. If the army carries out its tasks, then the civilian authorities, the people who are in charge of that, can carry out their tasks. But I would like to stress that events went in quite another direction, contrary to all of our expectations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these possible incidents, the 450 members under your command were not able to resolve them; is that so?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not part of our task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me: In paragraph 3 of this order, it states that "The detachment, headed by its command, stood on the defence of humanity, togetherness, and neighbourly solidarity as indestructible indication or characteristic of Bosanski Samac, determined at any price to defend those values to the last, defend them and succeed in that." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do apologise, Your Honour. My co-counsel just informed me that there's something missing from the transcript, but it's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could you please tell me: The last paragraph on page 1, divisions and separation which pushed the peoples and the ethnic groups into fear, hopelessness, and impotence, have given birth to armed all peoples detachment as an all peoples power, which by hard and honourable battle has managed to establish control over all the vital points and facilities in town. These are probably the post office, the radio, the waterworks. Are those the vital facilities that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th, in the evening, the command secured some of these key facilities, and those are the waterworks, so that people can have good, clean water; that is the bakery, which was to provide food for the members, i.e. bread; this also includes the health centre, as the facility which is there to provide assistance and aid to people, to the elderly, the sick, the wounded. Of course, there were other key facilities also. But in any case, the 4th Detachment did not provide its members for the securing and protection of facilities, the ones who were performing duties in the civilian sphere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You secured Radio Samac as well, didn't you? That's also a key facility, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the radio is one of those facilities which we also believed should be placed in the service of the citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course you secured it so that there would be no surprises.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We carried out this task, but I don't know whether it was on the 17th or the 18th that each of these key facilities was secured. I cannot claim something like that happened that very night on the 17th, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you started the process of weapons collection, as you told Mr. Pisarevic, and the securing of these key facilities, I must admit, you did that quite professionally. The 4th Detachment did this in quite a professional way. The 4th Detachment took upon itself the responsibility for law and order in Samac.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We took upon ourselves those activities which needed to be carried out in order to secure our unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the 4th Detachment, together with the volunteers and the Serb police, took over control of the key facilities; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police and the volunteers did not secure these key facilities together with members of the 4th Detachment. This was a task given to members only for those key facilities which were essential for the functioning of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. That's not what I'm saying. You received an order from the 17th Tactical Group together with the volunteers and the police to take over the key facilities during the night between the 16th and the 17th; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. The 17th Tactical Group never gave any orders to the 4th Detachment for any kind of activity during the night between the 16th and the 17th. Please, please. Don't make it seem like there was something that never actually took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm merely asking. I'm merely asking. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you definitely have the right to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2 of this announcement, paragraph 1 reads: "That's why the detachment calls upon all honourable people to join in and to comply with the instructions of its command concerning the organisation of life and work and the preservation of peace and order in Bosanski Samac." You agree with that; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We called upon all citizens, all the people who shared the convictions of the command of the 4th Detachment, to join in, and they did. I must say, many people did join in. They joined the 4th Detachment, precisely with the intention of preserving the town, of preserving its people, of preserving the property. We believed that there was safety in numbers and that numbers would help us the better to carry out our task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have no doubts about that, Mr. Antic. But tell me: The command of the 4th Detachment passed certain, or rather, adopted certain orders on the way life and work were organised; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we set decisions or instructions, we meant something quite different. Those were not laws governing life in Samac. These were simply our views and convictions which the command of the 4th Detachment then articulated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The decision on the introduction of the state of emergency was one such document, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. The 4th Detachment had nothing to do with the introduction of the state of emergency. It had no part in that. None of our members took part in that, not at any point in time. This was a document passed exclusively by the civilian bodies of authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, if you could be precise. When you say that the state of emergency was a document passed exclusively by the civilian bodies of authority, can you say which body specifically you're talking about, if you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Antic, whatever concern the preservation of law and order, you try to do your job the best way possible, the collection of weapons, to keep the risk down, to collect the weapons that were unlawfully owned, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, in as far as the activities of the 4th Detachment are concerned, in terms of the safety of its own members. We cared about preserving every single life, of our own members and of the citizens of Samac. When there was something we couldn't do, this invariably did not depend on us, on the command of the 4th Detachment; it was beyond our sphere of competence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last paragraph of this announcement reads: "According to the provocators spawned by the ugly policies of nationalist parties -- national parties, the policies of national parties, and fascist separatism, aided by international fascism, those who still incite to hatred and fratricide, the detachment will show no -- will have no mercy for them." As the detachment put its name under this announcement, tell me, what exactly did you mean by international fascism?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During those three days, the 17th, the 18th, and the 19th, the 4th Detachment believed that what was going on in Samac was the reflection of policies pursued by national parties. At that moment, we believed, as we were convinced that we should preserve Yugoslavia the way it was, or in a different form, that we should aid the JNA in its efforts to carry out its own aims. We were convinced that international relations affected the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean international fascism?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, globally. You couldn't say international fascism, but some forms were present in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, and they contained some of those elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, on page 18, line 15 and 16, it should be a part of my question which started on line 9, and then the answer of this witness is starting on the line 17. Just for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antic, the last sentence there, we'll have no mercy to spare for such people. Did you mean arrests? Did you mean actually killing those people? What did you mean by no mercy? Because you were an armed unit, after all, the detachment.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The detachment believed that should any armed clashes break out, and if the detachment were in a position to carry out anything like that, they would not have had mercy. But not in the sense of expulsion and humiliation of other people, but only if the detachment came into a position to engage in armed combat, then we would have had no mercy, because we considered ourselves capable of carrying out certain military tasks given us by our Superior Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, you practically got involved in armed combat. You started shooting. There was fighting in Samac. You were fighting with Croats. That was on the 17th of April, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The combat task of the 4th Detachment began on the 17th, around 9.00. We came out to the line, to our line of responsibility, to secure Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you joined with the volunteers and the Serbian police from Samac in defending the town, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The 4th Detachment did not cooperate in any such manner with the police or the volunteers. Rather, we had our own specific tasks which we simply carried out. This statement is simply out of the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to read to you now another statement based on some of my research and tell me whether you agree or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you read, is it from the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. No. This is just, I would say, conclusion, thesis of what we heard here during the proceedings and I would like just to hear the position of this witness with regard to the suggestion that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Antic, by way of conclusion, right, do you agree with what I'm about to read to you: In view of the fact that several other units took part in liberating the town from the 17th Tactical Group, units from the 17th Tactical Group, the role of the 4th Detachment in liberating the town in less than 24 hours is beyond dispute, its role in preventing major bloodshed, because only three people were killed in the liberation of the town. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If I told you, for example, that your assistant for security, Simo Zaric, in an interview for the Novi Sad TV, said that there was intelligence information that an attack on Samac had been prepared by Croats and Muslims between the 16th and the 17th or the 17th and the 18th of April, would you agree with me that he must have been right, since he was, after all, an intelligence officer, and he released this information in an interview to Novi Sad TV?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what intelligence exactly Mr. Zaric had. It is on account of that that I cannot comment on his assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Antic: As my client, Dr. Blagoje Simic, gave me precise instructions regarding the questions I'm about to ask you: Blagoje Simic claims that on the 17th of April he did not call Stevan Nikolic on the phone, nor through any other communications equipment, and he believes that you were not telling the truth when you said that you had received information that he had called Nikolic. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't talk about information that my commander may have had. I can only talk about what he informed us on. I was not the only person present. There were other people there too, and Mr. Zaric was among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Furthermore, my client believes and claims that the Crisis Staff did not even exist during the night between the 16th and the 17th of April, and he believes that what you said was simply not true, the information you provided in your testimony before this Tribunal. Are you prepared now to set your testimony right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Furthermore, my client claims that the Crisis Staff did not issue the order regarding the defensive operation between the 16th and 17th of April, but rather, that this was issued by the command of the 17th Tactical Group and the 4th Detachment. Are you ready to review your testimony as regards that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I gave you the sequence of events exactly as it was. I told you everything I did on the 17th, in the morning, and then later, in the course of the 17th and the 18th and as late as the 23rd, while I was commander. I did everything that I did pursuant to orders by the commander of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By way of conclusion, I will suggest the following: It is my belief that the 17th Tactical Group and the 4th Detachment, together with the Serb volunteers and the Serb police, took complete control over life and work in Samac, beginning with the 17th of April and onwards. Do you agree with that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th Tactical Group took control of what it was responsible for. The command of the 4th Detachment took control of what it was supposed to take control of in terms of its task, its task as given in the order by the commander of the 17th Tactical Group. So from the 17th on, the detachment was carrying out orders of the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, from the 17th -- from the morning of the 17th on, from the moment that the commander called me and issued the orders, and then on -- while we were carrying out our combat task, and then until 9.00, when I was given the order on the engagement of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 9.00 on the 17th of April on everything within the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment was controlled by the 4th Detachment, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 4th Detachment was in control of the line of its own responsibility, but it had no influence on life in the town of Samac. That was completely the responsibility of civilian authorities. The 4th Detachment had nothing whatsoever to do with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Antic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Now the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, this document D28/4 is not admitted into evidence yet, so it's a document ID. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: No objection to its admission, on the Prosecution's part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that -- well, I don't know who is entitled, Your Honour. Maybe if it's ID, maybe my learned friends should be entitled to tender it into evidence, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If this is a proper moment, I have to admit that I didn't pay much attention to this. But could we have now, since the witness identified the document, read it, and if there is not any objection from the Prosecution side, we might admit it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We just have confirmation that it will retain the same number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be treated as Exhibit D28/4 and D28/4 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please. Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I have some questions for you on behalf of the Prosecution. My name is Di Fazio. It's in both our interests if you could keep your answers as brief as possible. If you do that, the whole exercise could be finished in a fairly short period of time, I hope. I just want you to restate again the objectives of the JNA, the 17th Tactical Group, and the 4th Detachment. You agree that one of the purposes of the JNA was the protection of the population and the people?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree that one of the purposes of the 17th Tactical Group, or rather, the purposes of the 17th Tactical Group were to prevent war from spilling over from Croatia into Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of the basic, fundamental tasks of the 17th Tactical Group and the 4th Detachment was to transfer war [as interpreted] into Bosnia and Herzegovina through the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group and the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The way your answer comes out was translated in English is not entirely clear. You agree that one of the fundamental tasks of the 4th Detachment was to prevent any incursions from Croatia or war spilling over from Croatia into the territory of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you agree that another purpose of the 4th Detachment was the prevention of interethnic strife?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have a correction of the answer in line 12 of the witness, where he says: "Yes, one of the basic fundamental tasks of the 17th Tactical Group and 4th Detachment was to transfer war." That's what the transcript has. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, the way your answer -- one of your earlier answers was translated was this: I was asking you about the basic purposes of the 17th Tactical Group, and you said, at least the way it's been translated: "One of the basic, fundamental tasks of the 17th Tactical Group and 4th Detachment was to transfer war into Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, I don't think that's correct and I don't think that's what you meant to say. Can you just tell us what you did say, for the purposes of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The transfer of war operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And the purpose of the 4th Detachment was to prevent the transfer of war operations from Croatia into the territory of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations, according to military terminology, are a wider concept. Since the 4th Detachment had a small area of responsibility, you could not talk about an operation. We talked about the transfer of activities, because activities is a much narrower concept in military terminology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. I understand. But as far as the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment was concerned, one of its tasks was to prevent war breaking out in Bosanski Samac, war being transferred from Croatia into Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another object of the 4th Detachment was to secure property and protect property in Bosanski Samac, property of the people?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to protect the citizens and to protect their property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition, it was the role of the 4th Detachment to prepare for defence action in the event of a Croatian attack?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The detachment's task was to begin to act in the case of any military attack on the town of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber: If these principle objectives were also shared by the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th Detachments operating in areas nearby.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received our tasks from the command of the 17th Tactical Group, and since all the detachments were part of the 17th Tactical Group, the tasks were the same or specific to a particular area. The specific thing for the 4th Detachment was the fact that Bosanski Samac has a mixed population, where the majority of the population were Muslims, then Serbs, then Croats. In other areas where the detachments were formed, there were pure communities. So therefore, the tasks were not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The tasks -- are you saying that the tasks of part of these formations of the JNA were based on ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was, in fact, of mixed composition, which was a reflection of the structure of the population in Bosanski Samac. So it was specific in terms of its organisation and its tasks, precisely because it was -- because the population was mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question in this way, Mr. Antic: These other detachments that I've mentioned - the 1st, 2nd, and so on - their tasks was to protect personal property, protect the people, prevent incursion of war or fighting operations from the territory of Bosanski Samac, and they had responsibilities for those tasks irrespective of the ethnicity of the people who resided in their territories or theatre of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each detachment received the tasks to protect the population and their property in their area of responsibility. But I emphasise: The 4th Detachment had exceptionally complex tasks, precisely because of the population structure in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In preparing to carry out these tasks or these challenges that might face the 4th Detachment, the 4th Detachment organised training, do you agree, the target practice, in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It did have training, and it did have target practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It ensured that its members were armed, weapons were distributed from Pelagicevo to all its members?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th Tactical Group provided weapons and uniforms that were necessary for the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I would like to stress that there wasn't enough of either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. In addition, the 4th Detachment established a system of patrols in the area of Bosanski Samac, and the purpose of those patrols was to provide intelligence to the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were they first established, these patrols?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The patrols were established in early February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was a system put in place whereby, if anything untoward happened, if anything out of the ordinary happened, these patrols would report to you, to the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The patrols were obliged to inform the 4th Detachment command about all important events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this system of patrols was set up precisely to enable the 4th Detachment to cope with a sudden attack?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The patrols were given tasks to inform the command about all significant events related to the existence of the 4th Detachment and its activities which it would undertake in certain circumstances. However, the detachment could not make the decision by itself. I mean the detachment command. But they informed the command of the 17th Tactical Group of all significant events, which in turn would set the tasks that the 4th Detachment needed to carry out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The territory of Croatia begins across the Sava River, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A matter of some hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's about four to five hundred metres across the Sava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was a bridge at Bosanski Samac linking it with the territory of Croatia on the night of the 16th and 17th?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a bridge. It's a railway and vehicle traffic bridge between Samac and the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And although it may seem perfectly obvious, I wish to ask you this: Any attack would not be signalled to you; it would be a surprise attack? That goes without saying, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, in accordance with military strategy, any side which has offensive intentions tries to carry out the activities against the other side with as much of a surprise element as possible, and this is what the history of war to date has shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber, then, the contingency plans that the 4th Detachment had to cope with an unexpected and surprise attack in the middle of the night, from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment, under my command, did not have any contingency plans. It had a strictly determined or a strictly set task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I know what the tasks are. We've just discussed them and you've told the Trial Chamber what the tasks of the 4th Detachment were. One of them was to protect against attack. You agree that attack can be surprise attack. Please tell the Chamber what plans the 4th Detachment had to cope with a surprise attack, since that was one of its tasks, to cope with a surprise attack.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the conditions today, in contemporary conditions, it's very difficult to carry out a surprise attack. That is the objective, but very often, in view of intelligence data which each side takes steps to obtain, this is so. So the detachment would have the possibility to engage in case of a surprise attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that you were confident that there was going to be no surprise attack?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the command, we were convinced that there would be no surprise attack against Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. I may return to this topic later. I now want to move on to another topic, that is, the arrival of the paramilitaries or volunteers, as you have called them. They arrived at Batkusa, I think, on the 11th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They arrived at Batkusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I think that's the date as well, isn't it, the 11th of April?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Soon, very soon thereafter, you became aware, did you not, that they had arrived in a military helicopter?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I found out that they arrived in two helicopters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Military, JNA helicopters?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were military helicopters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that that immediately established in your mind a connection between the volunteers and the military, the JNA, otherwise they wouldn't be on JNA helicopters.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what channels they were and what kind of engagement, but we were convinced that they were not representatives, i.e. soldiers who arrived in those helicopters. In a military sense, that would not be a significant number for our area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me approach the issue in this way: These men who arrived on the JNA or military helicopters were camouflaged, they were known as the Sareni, and they were heavily armed, and that was well known?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were -- yes. They were in camouflage uniforms, wearing -- with firearms. This is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So you knew that these were features of their arrival: They came on military helicopters, they were heavily armed, wearing camouflage, combat uniforms. That indicates that they're soldiers, doesn't it, and that they are soldiers associated in some way with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since there were about 25 of them, and because of the fact that they were in camouflage uniforms, this is what was evident in that sense. But I claim that in a military sense, this small group did not represent any military unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my conclusion, since I'm familiar with military issues and also the military strategy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I've led you to the -- what I say to you are the indications that these were military men associated with the JNA, the fact of their being armed, the fact of their being uniformed, the fact that they are arriving in military JNA helicopters. What do you point to to lead you -- that leads you to something other than that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of the fact that they came in military helicopters, that they were wearing camouflage uniforms, and in view of their numbers. As far as the army is concerned, this was not a number which would constitute any kind of reinforcement that could come to this area. So my information indicated that even in spite of the fact that they came on military helicopters, these were not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So it's only the question of numbers that makes you draw that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on the number. At that first moment of my realisation, I felt that they were not soldiers and that there were completely different objectives in question there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you air those views with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not air those views. This was something that I, as an officer and commander of the 4th Detachment, was led to believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Even before the night and the events of the 16th and 17th, these paramilitaries or volunteers were already creating havoc. They were drinking heavily, stopping buses, and robbing people. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear of such occurrences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you -- sorry. Just remind the Chamber: How far is Batkusa from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Batkusa is 13 kilometres away from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So it's reasonably close. The 4th Detachment was, therefore, faced with a group of men who were already exhibiting extremely dangerous behaviour and who were heavily armed, who had already attacked property by robbing people. What plans did the 4th Detachment make to cope with and deal with this game?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before you answer, I object to this question. First of all, as far as we have evidence in this trial, there was another detachment in Batkusa, and it wasn't in the zone of responsibility of the 4th Detachment. So maybe this -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'll rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know, Mr. Antic, that Batkusa may not have been in the zone of responsibility of the 4th Detachment. However, as you've said, it was only 13 kilometres away and people can move; they can walk and they've got cars and so on. So you knew that in the area, in the area of Bosanski Samac, there was a group of heavily armed men who were already attacking property, robbing people. What plans did the 4th Detachment make to deal with these men in the event that they came to Bosanski Samac and did the same thing there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group of armed men with firearms, not heavy weapons, was stationed in the village of Obudovac and not in Bosanski Samac, and if they did go in from the 11th to the 17th, so before this, these were probably individual events. But the group as such did not enter Samac. Perhaps they did individually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you if they actually came to Samac or entered Samac individually or as a group. I'm asking what plans you made, the 4th Detachment made, to deal with any trouble that these -- that this group of heavily armed men might cause in your zone or -- your zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment, by forming patrols, gathered information about events which could be of interest or of significance for the activation of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which particular detachment was responsible for the areas of Batkusa and Obudovac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the 1st Detachment was responsible for Batkusa, and as far as I remember, I think the 5th [Realtime transcript read in error "4th"] Detachment was responsible for Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as commander of the 4th Detachment, did you contact the command --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One second. One second. One second. We have something here in the transcript. The witness said the 5th Detachment, not the 4th Detachment. So it makes significant difference. On line 22. MR. DI FAZIO: That's what I heard as well. That's what I heard over the earphones, at least. I think it's just the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have it corrected. MR. DI FAZIO: We all agreed it's the 5th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said the 5th was responsible for Obudovac; correct? Can you just say yes or no so that the transcript picks up your voice rather than just nodding, Mr. Antic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell the Chamber if you made any efforts to contact the commanders of those detachments and make inquiries as to the purpose of these volunteers being present in the area.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any contact with the commanders in these areas of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, it's 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break and continue at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution is continuing. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. If Your Honours please, just before I do, could I -- there's a degree of uncertainty on the part of the Prosecution as to precisely what hours we're sitting today, and it would assist us to plan for the remainder of the day if we could know exactly what the hours are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The schedule shows -- we are sitting up to 1330 and then we continue in the afternoon from 1500 hours to 1630. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, maybe this is not a good time, but before we begin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was about to say that. Can we complete the cross-examination first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before the break, Mr. Antic, I was asking you about contact with the -- or rather detachments, so to speak, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd detachments, and you told us that you made no effort to contact them, with a view to finding out about the purpose of the volunteers or the paramilitaries, what their purpose was in the area. Why didn't you contact them and ascertain what their purpose was, given that they had all those features that we've described: Being armed, carrying out robberies, and so on?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had no contacts with the detachments in whose area of responsibility of responsibility they had landed, nor with the commander for that particular area where they were staying. I had no contacts because I believed that the command of the 17th Tactical Group was familiar with all that. And had there been any need for steps to be taken, the command of the 17th Tactical Group would certainly have informed me. They would have organised certain meetings in connection with that occurrence for these reasons that I've spoken about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you believed that the command of the 17th Tactical Group was familiar with all of that. First of all, what were your reasons for believing that the 17th Tactical Group was familiar with all of that; and secondly, what do you mean precisely when you say "they were familiar with all that"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean that the command of the 17th Tactical Group knew about the occurrence, because they had their own bodies who were responsible for that, for gathering information, for forwarding the information to the command. I also informed the command about what I knew, and as I said, I found out from certain persons from my town. In the first two or three days, I can't locate the date exactly, I did have personal contact with them, or rather, they stopped me near my house, the house where I was born, and they checked or, rather, searched me and members of my family, as well as the boot of our car. They opened the boot of the car that I was driving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What information did you forward to the command of the 17th Tactical Group regarding these paramilitaries, and how did you forward it to it? Was it by way of official communique, letter, informal chat? How did you do it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our information concerning the group concerned mainly the fact that they landed in the area. Likewise, we had our own line, or rather, my assistant commander for intelligence and information, Mr. Zaric also had this information and the reasons or information about these reasons or information we would inform the command of the 17th Tactical Group. We informed them about the fact that they had arrived, that they were there, that citizens were being maltreated, stopped and searched, and so on and so forth, whatever we were able to find out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And this was done in some official manner, through your assistant commander for intelligence and security, Mr. Zaric, and from him on to the command of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Zaric informed, in his own capacity, about these data, as the command of the 17th Tactical Group had its own chief of intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you made this -- provided this information in an official manner, so to speak. What was the reaction of the 17th Tactical Group when you informed them that there was this bunch of heavily armed paramilitaries operating in the area and already robbing and threatening people? What did they tell you to do about them, or how did they respond?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we informed the command of the 17th Tactical Group about these occurrences, the command informed us that they had already had that particular piece of information. They told us this was not the first they heard of it, the information they received from the 4th Detachment. They had already known about it. As this group was not within the zone of responsibility of the 4th Detachment, the 4th Detachment did not need to take any steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So you were told by the command of the 17th Tactical Group that the 4th Detachment was not to do anything about the paramilitaries, and you were told this before the 16th?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that respect, the command ordered us explicitly that this was not our responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Who precisely in the command issued those orders?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, Colonel Lieutenant Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he communicate those orders to you personally or did he do so through Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order came through Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he, in turn, informed you, and that's how you knew that inaction was the order of the day as far as the paramilitaries were concerned?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric informed me about everything he learnt, as I was the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as inaction is concerned, inaction was the result of that particular group simply not being within the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the specific order that you have just testified about, namely, that the 4th Detachment do nothing?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe my colleague could ask this question again. I believe that the witness didn't understand that it was a question, actually. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry. I'll clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wasn't commenting, Mr. Antic. I was actually asking you a question. You said that inaction was the result of this group of paramilitaries not being within your area of responsibility, and I put to you that in addition, inaction was required because that was the specific order that you received from the command, from Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order would have been there if there had been any measures to be taken related to occurrences that might ensue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So then you tell the Trial Chamber of your knowledge of any orders that the other detachments had to deal with these paramilitaries in the days before the 16th and 17th. Did you see the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, or 5th Detachment arresting them, locking them up, taking them on in any way?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. I believe that the witness already said that he had no contacts with other detachments. That was during cross-examination of my learned colleague. So how could he possibly know what were -- I mean, it's pure speculation. MR. DI FAZIO: No, no. It's not -- my question is, as Mr. Re kindly pointed out to me: Did you see them? And my question is directed towards any direct knowledge that this witness has of any activities that those other detachments undertook in respect of these paramilitaries before the 16th. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the witness can answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Or indeed if he heard of anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So may I rephrase the question, if Your Honours please. Mr. Antic, did you see or hear of anything that the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, or 5th Detachment did to deal with the activities of these paramilitaries in the days before the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information that any of the detachments took any measures, nor did I know whether they had received any order along these lines from the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the undertaking of military operations by the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th Detachment is something that you should have been kept aware of; it's something that was -- it's necessary for you to know what activity they're conducting for you to simply carry out your duties as commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty to undertake certain military activity on the part of another detachment does not automatically mean that certain activities or combat operations should be undertaken by the 4th Detachment. Therefore, the order for the 4th Detachment could only have been issued by the commander of the 17th Tactical Group and not by any parallel units that were active, that were operating in our area, and that were part of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. All I meant, Mr. Antic, was this: If the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, or 5th Detachments were undertaking any significant military operation, such as engaging in conflict with a band of 30 or so armed men, as a matter of necessity it would be important to notify all the other detachments that this military operation was being conducted, so that you know what's going on, you know how to react and deal with what's going on in neighbouring zones of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is the reflection of the system of command in the JNA. Therefore, the 4th Detachment is only responsible to the command of the 17th Tactical Group for any activity that is undertaken. So this has nothing to do with activities by another detachment. And certainly, the command of the 17th Tactical Group would not have missed the opportunity to issue certain orders, if orders were called for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I fully understand the principle of subordination, and I fully understand that your command was in the 17th Tactical Group. I understand all that. All I'm simply asking you is this: It would have been necessary if any of the neighbouring detachments, that is, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, or 5th Detachments, undertook a major military operation, it would have been necessary to notify you, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a matter of assessment, and I can't go into that. I can't tell you what's necessary and what's not. But in a specific situation, it is the Superior Command that issues orders to me, and they tell me according to their own assessment how important the events about to take place are or the events that had already happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Let's move to another topic now. You know, don't you, that on the 29th of February, 1992, a decision was taken on the formation of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I learned this from the media, the fact that the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac had been established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that the SDS was the driving force behind the creation of that particular institution or body?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that on the 28th of March, a session was held at Obudovac, where various Serbs were appointed to various positions in this new municipality, this new Serb municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about the assembly, or rather, the meeting. But as for its specific conclusions or the views expressed there, I did not really have any opportunity to read about them anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the formation of this Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac and its work in creating -- in making appointments to various positions in March of 1992 were well known throughout the community; it was a matter of common knowledge in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Most citizens knew about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, most citizens knew that the driving force behind the creation of this entity was the SDS?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the appointments was the police chief, Stevan Todorovic. He was made police chief on the 28th of March, I think.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm familiar with the fact that Stevan Todorovic was police chief in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was, in effect, a second or shadow government that was being created on the territory of Bosanski Samac, the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was a shadow government, I don't have any such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that it had declared a Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, you knew that appointments had been made to various positions in this institution, and you knew that at the time that this was going on, there was already in existence a democratically elected municipality of Bosanski Samac, so therefore, what was being created was a shadow government; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And its clear that that institution, the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, was a body that represented Serbs; it did not represent Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it represented Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was contrary to the Yugoslav idea of representation in governing bodies for members of all ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was contrary to the expectations of the majority of Bosanski Samac population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was contrary to the Yugoslav ideal of participation in government and administration by members of all three ethnic groups, because it represented Serbs only; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
