utterances.text: Yes, those of Yugoslav orientation, the citizens who were committed to that, who wanted a life together, of all citizens in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you know that this body, the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, appointed a Crisis Staff just before the 16th and 17th of April, 1992, the Crisis Staff that was headed throughout its life by one of the defendants in this case, Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in particular, you know that it was created before the 16th and 17th?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, I heard when the Crisis Staff was first heard of through its proclamation, and I think this was on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If I said to you that the Crisis Staff was formed in the St. Sava Hall of the church of the holy mother in Obudovac on the 15th [Realtime transcript read in error "18th"] of April, 1992, does that spark your memory, refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. -- before the witness answers, your question -- the transcript shows 18th of April. Is that the date you mentioned? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if I did mention the 18th, I was wrong, and I certainly meant the 15th of April. Let me -- perhaps if I just rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, if I say to you that the Crisis Staff was formed in the St. Sava Hall of the Church of the Holy Mother in Obudovac on the 15th of April, 1992, does that refresh your memory as to the date of its creation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a citizen of Samac, and I cannot decisively speak about that date, because I didn't have any specific knowledge in terms of that date. I would like to underline that the first time that I became aware of the existence of the Crisis Staff was in terms of the announcement that the Crisis Staff issued. I heard clearly, with my own ears, the announcement, i.e., that there was a Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you admit of the possibility that it was created before the 15th -- before the 16th; it's just that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection. Maybe my learned friend can rephrase the question. What does it mean, this formation? Admitted the possibility -- MR. DI FAZIO: I withdraw the question, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's calling for speculation. MR. DI FAZIO: I withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 16th and 17th of April, you agree, don't you, that the existing institutions of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, the democratically elected assembly, was extinguished?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This act meant that the democratic institutions had ceased to operate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this democratic institution had represented up until that point Serbs, Croats, and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In an earlier period, there were institutions which had as its members people from all of the three ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The new civilian administration that replaced it was a Serb-only administration, that is, it consisted of Serbs and represented the interests of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the general population picture at the time, in April of 1992, was that Serbs consisted of less than 50 per cent of the population?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the census of 1991, I know that there were 2.200 Muslims living in the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, if I might briefly interrupt you. I don't need the full demographic details. That's okay. All I'm asking you is a very simple thing, a very simple matter: Serbs consisted of less than 50 per cent, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a little bit under 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Following the 16th and 17th, within the first month and a half, arrests started of the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prisons were created in the SUP, the TO building, the high school gym, and in the primary school. That's all starting fairly quickly after the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within a month, a paramilitary, Lugar, had slaughtered 14 or 15 people in a warehouse at Crkvina, and that was well known in the town, 15 or so non-Serbs, I should say.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with that fact. I personally felt that that was a major stain on the reputation of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In addition, within that period of a month and a half after the 16th of April, Croats were isolated and taken to Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was apparent to you, wasn't it, within a very short period of time, what the nature of this new civilian administration in Bosanski Samac truly was?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a man and at that point the commander -- a former commander of the 4th Detachment, we strongly condemned that occurrence. We were against that policy, against the arrest of members of any ethnic group. As far as we were able to, as members and as people, we did as much as we could, but some circumstances exceeded our abilities, and my own case shows that the command of the 4th Detachment was also under considerable pressure. It was terrorised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But within the first month and a half, it was plain to you that the nature of this new civilian administration was such that it was going to be -- that it was conducting an attack on the non-Serb population: Arrests, isolation, murders by the paramilitaries, not to mention the extinguishment of the existing democratically elected structures?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those events were reality in the life and the fate of our citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so -- I withdraw that. The reality is that those matters that I've raised with you, Mr. Antic, the reality is that those matters that I've raised with you indicate a campaign of persecution directed towards the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown P127, please, the B/C/S version, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before we look at the document, Mr. Antic -- Mr. Antic, just before we look at the document, just one other question that I need to raise with you following from your last answer, is that the campaign of persecution that you have agreed was taken place was conducted, effected, carried out, by the Crisis Staff, the Serbian police, and the Serbian paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I'm familiar with the structure of the jurisdiction, orders relating to these events, according to what I know, are adopted by the Crisis Staff and the internal affairs body is the body that carries out those tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you agree, don't you, that the campaign of persecution that you have agreed was being conducted was being carried out by those -- that group of three that I've mentioned: The Crisis Staff, paramilitaries, and the Serbian police? I don't need a detailed administrative explanation. Just you agree, don't you, that those three groups were carrying out the persecution?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Ms. Usher. You may leave. I'll be a little while on the document, if you want to return to your seat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, this document, are you already acquainted with it? Have you had a chance to look at it before you started your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we have it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this document. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And perhaps I do need the assistance of the usher after all. Can it be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, the document is relatively easy to read because it's divided into paragraphs, and if you just skim through the text of it, you'll come to the fifth paragraph. If you could just find the fifth paragraph. Mr. Antic, you're looking at the screen rather than the document. The document is there on that machine called the ELMO. Have a look at the document, pick it up. You can touch it. And just find the fifth paragraph. It's on page 2 of the English, so I suppose thereabouts in the B/C/S. All right? Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you see there that -- oh, and sorry, before I proceed. You know that Mr. Zaric is one of the authors of this document, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the 2nd Posavina Brigade, which was formed in the reorganisation of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Mr. Zaric is one of the people who worked to compile this document, in accordance with the function that he was carrying out at the time in the 2nd Posavina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Antic. Now look at the fifth paragraph, and you see there that the document claims that with the blessing of those who brought them in, that is, the paramilitaries, the commandos, they engaged in unheard of looting of private and socially owned property, which was then transferred back to Yugoslavia. Do you see that portion? Do you see that? Just tell me --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you agree, don't you, that those who brought them in was the -- included the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just at the beginning of the paragraph, there's reference to the liberation of Samac. It's in fact in the first sentence. Do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context, the liberation of Samac refers to the activities of the police and the paramilitary formations. That's the essence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was hardly a liberation, was it, Mr. Antic, given what you have said took place after the 16th. It wasn't liberation at all, was it, for the people of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, according to our information, the knowledge of the command of the 4th Detachment, it's not liberation. Samac cannot be liberated of its own citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And just while -- last question on that paragraph: There's an allegation here of looting. You have no reason to disagree with that allegation. That's in fact what was occurring in the period of time immediately following the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all the legal regulations, such activities are all treated as plunder. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. Would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The plunder that you referred to was in fact looting.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We treated it as looting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- sorry. Yes. You don't disagree, do you, that this activity of plunder and looting was taking place in the period of time immediately following the 16th, as it says in the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Madam Usher, I've finished with the document for the time being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Antic. Just the way the question was phrased, it's -- and the answer, it's not entirely clear. Let me put it to you as briefly as I can. You agree that plunder and looting was occurring after the 16th, in the territory of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'll return to these issues later, but I want you to direct your attention now to the actual takeover of the town itself on the night of the 16th and 17th. At 3.00 a.m., when you woke up, you had no idea who was carrying out the attack, did you? All you could hear was shooting?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that point, until I heard the shooting, I didn't have any information. After I woke up, got up and went to the command, then I found out about the events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was apparent that shooting was coming from within the town, within the area of the town itself?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The shooting was coming from within the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so therefore, this had all the hallmarks of an attack.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shooting were a hallmark of the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the only possible conclusion for you at that time was that the town was under attack?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My first thought was that an attack against Samac was taking place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the 4th Detachment do to cope with this attack?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first move that I, as a commander, was able to make was to order the officer on duty at the command to urgently call together the command, to the command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Friday, you testified that even before you went to see Mr. Nikolic, that is, while you were still in Bosanski Samac, you knew of sporadic fire fights within the town and that the focus of activity was on facilities and buildings within the town. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I heard shooting from within the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The situation was such, was it not, that the only choice that the 4th Detachment had, if it was to protect the people of Bosanski Samac, and if it was to protect the property within Bosanski Samac and the institutions within Bosanski Samac, to immediately go into action and defend the town? That was the only choice it had; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was not -- didn't have all its members in one place. This wasn't a barracks, so that I could take immediate steps. Therefore, my first task, in accordance with the order of the commander, was to mobilise the detachment and within that framework also to receive the appropriate order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was the only body that was capable of defending the town; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were convinced that the 4th Detachment was a force capable of defending the town of Samac from any kind of attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was the only body on that night, on the 16th and 17th of April, that was capable of defending the town from any kind of attack?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the 4th Detachment did not have all its members in one place. They slept at their homes on that particular night. Many of them were even outside Samac, and so on and so forth. Therefore, we were not organised in such a way as to be able to gather all our members in such a short time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get on to that topic later, but would you please just answer my question that I asked, and that's simply this: On that night, the only body capable of defending Bosanski Samac was the 4th Detachment; there was no one else who could do the job?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the task of the 4th Detachment, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And only the 4th Detachment could do it; there was no one else?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must point out: It was the task of the 4th Detachment. Therefore, we believed it was a military duty to do what was our task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You received your first concrete orders at 9.00 that morning, and that was in Pelagicevo, from Colonel Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fighting had started at 3.00 in the morning, so that's some six hours after the commencement of hostilities?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first shots were heard at 3.00 in the morning on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, was there anything to prevent you mobilising the 4th Detachment in anticipation of action to defend the town? And I ask you that because knowing that you could have communicated by wireless with the command at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would just like the clarification of this question, because even it is not quite clear to me. MR. DI FAZIO: Okay. I'll rephrase it. It wasn't -- I'll put it --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 3.00 in the morning, Mr. Antic, your wireless set was working and functioning perfectly well, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was working perfectly well the moment I entered the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And you had your patrols out carrying out their reconnaissance and intelligence duties?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first information we obtained related to the ongoing activities in the town itself came from our patrols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was nothing to prevent you mobilising the 4th Detachment, getting them ready for action as quickly as possible, and, at the same time, getting concrete instructions from Nikolic and the command of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was not my private army for me to mobilise at will. As I said, there is a very strong principle of subordination that is applied in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I realise that, and that's why I asked you about the wireless, you see. You could get ready to cope with this attack that was clearly, clearly under way by mobilising the 4th Detachment, and you could adhere to the principle of subordination at the same time, by getting on to the wireless, speaking to Nikolic, and saying: The town is under attack. I'm ready to deal with it. What do I do?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't issue any kind of order related to the engagement of the 4th Detachment without prior orders from a Superior Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand -- there was nothing, then, to prevent you from getting on to the wireless and seeking orders for immediate mobilisation from Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have to object. I mean, I don't have any problem, particular problem with this question, but isn't that what the witness already stated, that he called Superior Command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It's different, because the question is asking the witness whether it was possible for him to seek, yes, orders for immediate mobilisation from his own superior. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you contact Nikolic by radio?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I found out about the first shots being fired, I arrived at the command about half past 3.00. I did what my duty was, what my duty bade me do, once I found out about the things happening in Samac, I informed Commander Nikolic and I requested instructions from him as to what I should do in relation to the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what time was that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was about a quarter to 4.00, I believe, because we had obtained information at half past 3.00 at the command, and immediately after I had been informed, I in my turn informed Commander Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What information did you have?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been informed by our patrols. They told me about their observations. And they had observed police members in their uniforms and volunteers in their camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew that the town was under attack by a combination of men in camouflage uniforms and police?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told Nikolic that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his reaction was do nothing, or his orders were do nothing?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. His order was for me, as the commander, and Mr. Zaric as the assistant commander, to appear immediately, to come to him at the command building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But apart from telling you to get in the car and get on down to Pelagicevo, you got no orders from Nikolic in the 17th Tactical Group to do anything concrete about the attack that was under way?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No other order, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- yes. Thank you. What time did you actually leave to get to Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, about quarter past 4.00 or half past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So possibly up to three quarters of an hour after you spoke to Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the meantime, the attack was continuing -- you could hear fighting and shooting of weapons?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was still in the town, I did hear shooting, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was plain to you, therefore, that the inaction of the 4th Detachment at this stage was going to facilitate the activities of whoever it was that was attacking the town?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the steps that I was in charge of, according to the chain of command. Now, whether this made anything easy for someone, that's a totally different issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. But my question is simply this: It was plain to you that the longer the 4th Detachment did nothing, the greater the possibility of the attackers achieving their purpose?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is an assumption like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was your assumption, as commander of the 4th Detachment? Was that a worry that you had in your own mind?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as I heard sounds of shooting, I, as commander, got worried, because I had no idea what was going on, until I was given certain information, and then I understood what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What information were you given that stopped your worries?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never stopped worrying, worrying about the fate of the town itself. All members of the 4th Detachment sacrificed their own fate for the sake of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that, Mr. Antic. All I'm asking you, though, is this: You just said that you were given -- you were worried, as commander, until you were given some certain information. What information were you given?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, as commander, was worried throughout the war, especially during the period that -- where the fate of the town of Samac was being decided. Therefore, those events were contrary to the way the 4th Detachment envisaged the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That might be so. But just tell us: What information were you given that caused you to understand what was going on? What information was that? Who gave it to you? When did they give it to you, and what was it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information was crystal clear to the command of the 4th Detachment, once we have gathered. The information concerning the taking of Samac was also clear to all the members of the 4th Detachment, because that was not what the 4th Detachment had guaranteed to its citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I misunderstood you. Are you referring to the information that Nikolic gave you when you saw him at 9.00 at Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him at the command earlier, 9.00. That was his order for the 4th Detachment [as interpreted]. What confirmed this was information provided by a patrol to the 4th Detachment when the 4th Detachment gathered at half past 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't want to interrupt my colleague, but there seems to be some misunderstanding here in the transcript. On page 58, line 19, "I saw him at the command earlier." Then it goes 9.00. "That was his order for the 4th Detachment." It doesn't make much sense. Actually, he said that he saw him before 9.00. I believe that this can be clarified easily. MR. DI FAZIO: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw Nikolic before 9.00 at Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, at the command in Pelagicevo. Mr. Zaric and I arrived in the early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you this: You know a man named Fadil Topcagic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, he's Mr. Zaric's brother-in-law, I believe. You know the man I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Zaric is the brother-in-law of Fadil Topcagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Thank you. Did you see him on the morning of the 17th, before you went to Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him at the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he recount to you his experiences of that night?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment when Mr. Zaric and I set out for Pelagicevo, at the entrance, Fadil Topcagic came in. He was very agitated and he told us something along these lines: We said that we had already heard something about that, and then Mr. Zaric and I went to Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he had seen Mr. Todorovic and Serbian police and paramilitaries arming themselves and getting ready in the village of Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadil Topcagic, a little later on the same day, told me about his own fate. In order to console him, I told him that the police might as well have broken into my flat and taken me to some place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But I'm not talking about later in the day. But I'm talking about your contact with him -- your contact with him just before you set off to Pelagicevo to speak to Nikolic. At that time, did he provide you with any detailed information regarding Todorovic, the Serbian police, paramilitaries and what their objectives in the town were?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were leaving for Pelagicevo, he just told me in passing what was happening in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's the expression you used yesterday. He mentioned this to you in passing. Of course, you subsequently found out that he had been present in Crkvina -- MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had, in fact, been in Crkvina and had seen Todorovic and the police and the paramilitaries getting ready to come in and take over in Bosanski Samac, and he knew, what's more, what their objectives were, what particular buildings they were going to take and so on; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After I returned from Pelagicevo, he told not only me, but rather he said this at the command, that he had been taken to Crkvina by force and that there he was given a specific task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but when you were leaving to go, even before this, when you were leaving to go, before you received orders in Pelagicevo, you had an opportunity to speak to him. Did he not tell you then, report to you, in full detail, his experiences in going off to Crkvina and seeing all these preparations being made by the Serbian police and paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that moment, he only let us know what had happened. I said in passing that we already knew about that, and upon our return, he told us in more detail what he had been made to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It must have been immediately clear to you, even if he had told you only in passing, that here was a man who could provide detailed intelligence and information about the attack on the town. Now, surely that required you to debrief him, find out what he had seen and observed; if necessary, take him to Pelagicevo, so that you could have fresh, up-to-date, accurate, detailed information about this attack.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that occasion, I simply didn't have time to debrief him thoroughly. The hints he gave me of what he wanted to tell me were sufficient in themselves. I understood that I had to go to Pelagicevo immediately. This was an explicit order by Commander Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Zaric was there with you. Now, he's a man who knows the value of intelligence, isn't he? He's an experienced security man. He's worked in the security services and chief of police. Did he express any interest in this wealth of information as to what was going on, this wealth of information that Topcagic had?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that Topcagic was in possession of at that moment and that he wanted to share with us, we had already found out about that, because members of our patrols had arrived at the command and told us in detail exactly what was going on in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I'm sorry. I didn't realise that. So you knew that it was an attack on the town by Serbian police, you knew that it was an attack on the town by these paramilitaries who had arrived at Batkusa, and you knew which particular buildings and vital facilities they were going to target, the police station, the Silos, and so on, and you knew this even before you went to Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I did not know about that before I went to Pelagicevo, which particular buildings, which members of the police, or which paramilitaries, or rather, volunteers, and which would have been the buildings that they would go for first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: Would this be an appropriate moment, if Your Honours please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break and continue at 12.50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, between the 17th of April, 1992, and the day that you resigned, some days later, you received three orders, basically. One was to mobilise the 1st [sic] Detachment; two was to take up defensive positions around the Bosna and the Sava River; and three was the collection of weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. My learned colleague referred to 1st Detachment here on page 62, line 21. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry if I did. I didn't mean to. I'm of course talking of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were the three orders that you got; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were the three orders that the 4th Detachment should carry out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as far as the adoption of defensive positions was concerned, the purpose of that was to prevent any forces entering the town?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the task, to take the line of defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the 4th Detachment carried out that order, set up defensive positions, and continued to maintain those defensive positions in the days following the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positions, once the members of the 4th Detachment were deployed in that way, these positions were held and maintained until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while that particular order was being followed and activities were being conducted, in the town itself, the police and the volunteers and the Crisis Staff were going about their business of establishing the new Serbian municipality, establishing themselves?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was carrying out this order. Neither I nor anyone else went into the town. I personally was with the soldiers, at the defensive positions, and I was the one who personally deployed each one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand that. But as far as you're aware, while you were engaged on the defensive perimeter of the town, creating these defensive positions, the trenches, and so on, getting ready, in town, the Crisis Staff is busy at work consolidating its power, issuing orders, carrying on its business?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 4th Detachment was carrying out its order, its task, but by doing that, it did not make it possible for anyone else to be doing these other jobs, insider ones that were connected to the civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The result of the actions of the -- let me withdraw that. By adopting these defensive positions, any other forces were prevented from coming in and interfering with the activities of this Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By taking up these defensive positions, the 4th Detachment, by taking up the defence line, it was entrusted with the task of preventing any military formations from entering the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result, any other military forces doing anything about the creation of this new Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By carrying out this task, the 4th Detachment was specifically to prevent the entry of any military formations into town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And upsetting any of the activity of the Crisis Staff creating this new Serbian municipality? I'm not suggesting that's what you wanted to do, but that's the effect of what happened.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By looking at it from one aspect solely, this might seem that way. However, this was not the objective of any single member of the 4th Detachment. I've already told you what our commitment was and what our tasks were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I've heard you. I understand your evidence. I understand your evidence. But I'm not asking you about the objectives of the 4th Detachment. Was the 4th command -- were you, as commander of the 4th Detachment, and other members in the command of the 4th Detachment, concerned that the 4th Detachment's activities in setting up defensive perimeters around the town might be seen as assistance, perceived as assistance to the activities of the Crisis Staff in establishing the Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My objective and the objective of the command, as well as of the large number of the members of the 4th Detachment, was in terms of concern about what was happening in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. You were concerned about the creation and the establishment of the Serbian municipality.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were not in favour of that. We wanted to stay within Yugoslavia and not to be separated along ethnic, religious lines, or any other lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree, wouldn't you, that this order that you received from Nikolic to set up defensive perimeters meant that the Crisis Staff was able to carry out its activity of establishing the Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you viewed it in that way, you could reach such a conclusion. However, that was not the commitment either of the JNA or of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. I've got no quarrel with what you say. I've heard your evidence. I've heard you and I understand what you say. But regardless of what your objectives were, regardless of what the 4th Detachment objectives were, the fact of the matter is that by establishing defensive perimeters around the town, it facilitated the creation of this Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac. They were left free to carry on their work, and you couldn't do anything about it, because that was the order you received; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a strict order, and in that sense we carried it out. However, certain things started to develop in a different direction, so that the 4th Detachment and its members were not able to influence that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure that became apparent very quickly too, and it's something that you didn't agree with, did you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, let's just get back to this issue of defensive perimeters. Now, I'm not asking you -- we've heard your evidence about the objectives and your objectives of the 4th Detachment, but you have to agree, don't you, that the result of the order that was given to you by Nikolic to set up defensive perimeters permitted this Crisis Staff to carry on its business of establishing itself. I'm not saying that's what you wanted, but that's the effect of it. That was the result, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, if you look at it from the side, at a certain angle, you can come to such a conclusion. However, by deploying on this line of defence, as I said, we wanted to prevent the incursion of any other formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, as a Yugoslav, did not agree with the creation of this Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, or anything that permitted it to be created?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that that was not the commitment or the view of any single member of the command of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The second order that you got --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second order that you received on the 17th was disarmament, and you've told us about how you carried that out.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the order, and we believe that we successfully carried it out. It wasn't from the back, and there was no question of endangering the lives of the members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the exercise had been completed, it effectively meant that the population of the town, the citizens of the town, had been disarmed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only those weapons which the citizens of Samac were not allowed to possess in accordance with the laws.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The result was that it effectively meant, didn't it, that any resistance to the Serb -- the new Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac was going to be that much more difficult, any resistance by people in the town?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were concerned exclusively with the security of our members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, I understand what you say, and I've heard all your evidence, Mr. Antic, and I'm not taking issue with what you say about that, about your intentions. I understand that. But notwithstanding your intentions, regardless of your intentions, an effect of disarmament meant that the population was weakened in the sense that it would be unable to resist the continuing process of the creation of this Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The possession of illegal, meaning illegal weapons, was a reflection of the fact that the parties were arming the citizens, so it was not legal arming, but it was arming along the lines of party affiliation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By taking away weapons from the people, whether they were legally or illegally possessed, you're in effect helping the Crisis Staff consolidate its power in the town. I'm not saying that was your intention, but that was the effect of what you were doing.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment had no intention whatsoever by the fact of its existence or by the fact of its activities, of enabling the authorities to consolidate themselves, meaning the civilian authorities of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for telling us about the intention of the 4th Detachment, but that's not what I'm asking you. The effect, whether you wanted it or not, of disarming the population was to permit the Crisis Staff to consolidate its power. That was the effect of it. I'm not saying it's what you wanted.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another question of what the consequences were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right, and that's all I'm saying, Mr. Antic. That's all I'm saying. I understand your position as --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's also what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you agree, regardless of what your intentions were, and I've heard -- MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, we agree with you that you did not want to facilitate the consolidation of power by the Crisis Staff, but you agree that the result of disarming the population meant that the Crisis Staff could go ahead and consolidate its position?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this in no way was the intention of the 4th Detachment. There was no intention of anything like that at any point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The effect of the 4th Detachment disarming people meant that the population didn't have any arms, was disarmed, whereas the Serbian police and the volunteers were heavily armed, and that remained the situation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, we looked after the safety of our own members, and the amount of weapons that had been collected, illegally owned weapons, shows that the national parties had been very active in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th, the 4th Detachment was not the only organ that was going around collecting weapons. You agree that on that day, paramilitaries were also seizing weapons? I know they were doing it in a completely different way, but they were doing the same thing, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Members of the police, some of them, and the volunteers expropriated property, seized vehicles, and seized weapons too, of their own initiative, wherever they found weapons on the people that property was being taken away from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion in the command regarding the perception by the population of these two orders that you were carrying out: Disarmament and the setting up of defensive positions?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information that I had throughout the two days that this went on for, members of the 4th Detachment did not have a single incident in the course of their activity, which means that the order was being strictly complied with, the order of the 17th Tactical Group, and the command of the 4th Detachment governing the behaviour of the members. But this also means that those who monitored the implementation of these activities never had any hint or any indication that the order had been violated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday His Honour Judge Lindholm asked you -- sorry, Friday. My apologies. Friday. Judge Lindholm asked you if you were surprised that you received no order to defend the town, and in the course of answering that question, you said that you were hard hit by everything that was going on, the entire command of the 4th Detachment felt that way, and in a way, this was not in keeping with the objectives of the 4th Detachment. Now, what were you talking about when you -- MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that things were not in keeping with the objectives of the 4th Detachment, you were talking about the orders that you were given to carry out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, we did not agree with this entire activity related to the occurrences unfolding in Samac, starting with the activities between the 16th and the 17th, and continuing with the activities going on for over several days, and going in a totally negative direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Because -- thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. Would Your Honours just bear with me while I locate some notes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Antic, if your answer was yes or no, we may finish fairly quickly. You agree that, and I think you've already mentioned it this morning, that before the 17th of April, Serbs were less than 50 per cent of the municipality of Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree that on the night of the 16th and 17th of April, there was a takeover by Serb forces in Bosanski Samac? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree that a democratically elected municipal government that had existed was extinguished that night?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree that the new Serbian administration that was established excluded non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree that the takeover was conducted by Serbian police and Serbian paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've agreed that the Serb Crisis Staff took power and that the Serb paramilitaries and the police helped it to consolidate its power?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you agree, then, that the result of all of that is the takeover by one ethnicity, forcible takeover by one ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thereafter, what followed was that non-Serbs lost their right to participate in government?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already mentioned, and you agree, that arrests and detentions by Serb paramilitaries and the Serb government, the Serb municipal government, took place of non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree that the forcible takeover that you've just described, the arrests, detentions, and mistreatment that took place in Bosanski Samac by members of one ethnicity directed towards other ethnicity would cause interethnic strife?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you agree that the purpose of -- one of the purposes of the JNA was to prevent interethnic strife?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the objective.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you agree, from what you saw, that in Bosanski Samac the JNA was ordered not to interfere with this series of arrests, detention, and ethnic takeover?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment did not have any such orders, but it was certainly shaken by those events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, it received no orders to prevent the ethnic takeover that was taking place?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, the 4th Detachment, did not receive any orders concerning the engagement of the 4th Detachment except as it related to the very tasks that the 4th Detachment was supposed to perform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P164, the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, if you could just look at paragraph -- this is the factual basis for the plea agreement entered into by Biljana Plavsic. You know her, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, to go to paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection, on the basis that this is irrelevant for our case. That's number one; number two, that in indictment against Mrs. Biljana Plavsic, there is not any word about the municipality of Samac and events in Samac; and number three, this witness is not an expert that he can give any kind of opinion with regard to this plea bargain agreement; and number 4, this is absolutely without any relevance. It's an invalid document, because it's just a personal position of Mrs. Plavsic in connection with the agreement with the other party, with the Prosecution. None of these facts were challenged into the court of law during the cross-examination and with regard to the other corroborative evidence. I put these objections for the record and move to strike all questions with regard to this plea bargain agreement, today and during all previous testimonies of previous witnesses. Just for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is of the view that it's proper for the Prosecution to question the witness on the plea agreement as put before the witness. So the witness can go ahead and answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, it's 1.30. This shouldn't take me too much longer to wrap it up. Can I do that later this afternoon? I assume we're breaking now, aren't we, or is it 1.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are breaking off now and continuing in the afternoon at 1500 hours. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll wrap it up later this afternoon, if it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I address the Trial Chamber at this moment? Because I'm afraid it is a relatively urgent matter. Because during the previous break I spoke with my client. He just came from the medical examination. And he was again examined by Dr. Falke and his medical condition is not going better, and I was just informed by him that he won't be able to attend any afternoon sessions at all. Furthermore, Dr. Falke has said that he needs to rest and he's not allowed to have any physical activities, and it seems that his surgery that is scheduled for May will be necessary most probably in April. And some steps were undertaken in that respect. So Mr. Zaric is suffering more and more pain every single day, and I was informed by him that he really cannot attend afternoon meetings, particularly having in mind that there is one and a half hours of recess between the -- well, from 1.30 until 2.30, or whatever it is. But after that, and all this period, he cannot remain here, because he's really not in condition that is good enough for him to follow the whole day of trial. So I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber, on behalf of Mr. Zaric, that we remain on the schedule that was, up until last Friday, and this is maximum of time that he can spend here in the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that means that we can't proceed with the witness this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so, according to my instructions from Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: However, we'll go ahead and hold a Status Conference at 1500 hours. The accused need not be here. To reorganise the defence. It may be necessary to bring witnesses for the other accused and proceed and complete them, so that they don't have to wait unnecessarily for too long, when we have a courtroom available. So we'll adjourn. The proceedings will continue tomorrow morning. But we are having a Status Conference at 1500 hours with all the parties, without the accused being present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be followed by a Status Conference. The hearing will reconvene on Tuesday, the 18th day of March 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.34 p.m.,
